domain: Why the mid-century ergonomic case for designing workspaces around the average human body was intellectually coherent, and what understanding of labour we lost when individual variation reclaimed the design agenda.
topic: Why the mid-century ergonomic case for designing workspaces around the average human body was intellectually coherent, and what understanding of labour we lost when individual variation reclaimed the design agenda.

source.title: Woodrow Wilson’s Legacy Is Loaded With Good and Bad, but His Work to Even the Economic Playing Field Is Often Overlooked

movement.gist: Introduce the ergonomic mean-body doctrine: 1950s industrial engineers designed all workstations around statistical averages (elbow height, desk depth, chair angle), treating deviation as outlier noise. This was methodologically rigorous, empirically grounded, and became the basis for international workspace standards.

Steelman the approach: averaging produced reproducible, teachable, scalable systems; it enabled uniform safety protocols and reduced catastrophic design errors; it acknowledged that most workers clustered near the mean. The real intellectual move was treating the body as a measurable, optimizable system—not inferior to acknowledging variation, just prior to it.

Name the loss: by pivoting to 'inclusive design' and ergonomic customization, we abandoned the systematic study of how labour patterns actually distribute across populations; we lost institutional memory of what happens when a workspace must coordinate hundreds of bodies; we traded general knowledge for individual adjustment.

Withhold endorsement: the mean-body doctrine was not correct, and disability accommodation was genuine progress. But the cost was real—we no longer ask what organizing principle should replace the average if not the average itself.

primary.axis: standardization vs. particularity in human-centered design

poles: situated knowledge of how bodies actually work

tension_system.interaction: The triumph of variation-aware design rhetoric has obscured that we abandoned not just a false universalism but a genuine systematic understanding of labour itself—the cost of honoring difference is forgetting how work gets organized.

family_realization.note: Passage steelmans averaging brilliantly: 'Reproducible systems. Teachable ones.' grants real epistemic virtue while calling doctrine false. Endorsement trap present but resistible.

ending_behavior.note: 'The automated line is arriving' reopens the question structurally. 'We have forgotten the old answer' signals cost accrued, aperture widens to future necessity.
